lesson.title: Citing Sources: In-Text Citations and a Works Cited Entry
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: You know quoting and paraphrasing need a citation. Today: the actual format college-level writing uses to do it.

MLA style (one common college-prep citation format) uses two connected parts. An in-text citation appears right where you use the source, in parentheses, usually with the author's last name and a page number: (Smith 42). A Works Cited entry appears in a full list at the end of your paper, giving complete source details in a standard order: Author Last Name, First Name. "Title of Source." Container Title, Publisher, Year. These two parts work together — the in-text citation is a quick pointer, and the Works Cited entry gives the full information a reader would need to find that exact source themselves. Using your Day 2 source, write both a correct in-text citation and a correct Works Cited entry for it.
You now have every piece needed to use sources honestly and correctly: a strong question, credible sources, honest paraphrasing, and proper citation. Tomorrow we'll review the whole process together.

objectives: Write a correct MLA in-text citation
Write a correct MLA Works Cited entry with all required elements in order
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review Day 3's quoting/paraphrasing and why citations matter.
2. Introduce MLA in-text citation and Works Cited entry format together, showing how they connect.
3. Model writing both for one example source.
4. Have the child write both for their own Day 2 source.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide a fill-in-the-blank Works Cited template (Author Last, First. "Title." Container, Publisher, Year.) rather than requiring the format memorized from scratch
Ready for more: ask them to write an in-text citation and Works Cited entry for a source type WITHOUT a clear individual author (e.g. an organization's website)
This is genuinely a mechanical, format-following skill — precision matters more than creativity here, which is a different mode than most ELA lessons
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. An in-text citation is a short, parenthetical pointer (Author page#) placed where the source is used. 2. A Works Cited entry gives full source details (Author, Title, Container, Publisher, Year) at the end of the paper. 3. The two work together: the in-text citation points to the full entry, and the entry gives enough detail for a reader to find the source themselves.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Writing standard W.11-12.8: following a standard format for citation, completing the research-process foundation this unit builds toward a full research paper.
